question: Which Xbox-native unit-definition field owns normal production base cost, how is its effective value composed, and which bounded completion, display, and AI paths consume it?

scope.boundary: This topic closes the normal unit production factor, the separate ID-100-through-199 and ID-200-through-299 base-cost fields, the unit scalar, two cost wrappers, one completion threshold, the accepted rush-area display consumer, and two accepted AI input consumers. A later bounded packet identifies three building records and four non-unit UEA branches; complete record layouts and remaining identities, complete modifier composition, general UI or AI parity, downstream completion effects, runtime execution, and an implementation contract remain outside this topic.

composition: Start at ten; if the player-indexed value is positive, subtract it from ten.
If neutral condition 0x82CEF4E8(14) is nonzero, subtract one quarter of the current scalar with signed round-toward-zero arithmetic.
If unit-definition +0x50 bit zero is set and bonus 5 is active, subtract one half of the current scalar.
For unit types 10, 6, and 28, active bonus IDs 17, 33, and 34 respectively subtract one half of the current scalar. Bonus 33 remains semantically unresolved.
effectiveScalar.normalUnitCost: signed definition factor at +0x44 multiplied by the returned scalar, then divided by two with signed round-toward-zero arithmetic
effectiveScalar.qualification: Condition 14, the player-indexed halfword owner, and bonus 33 remain neutral. The helper handles only item IDs 0 through 99; this is static composition, not runtime proof. returnBoundary distinguishes entry owner, predicate-outgoing r4 and the later freshly sampled owner; original-owner attribution of optional bonus 5 requires the stated retention.

returnBoundary.question: What selected scalar return, stack-write and caller-retention contract can compose with the zero-amount CityUpdate call?
returnBoundary.callerJoin: Reuse the mode-one entry, signed population clamp and insufficient-production exit already recorded in occ-settler-production-gates.json. At 0x82D159C0/0x82D159C8, CityUpdate calls this helper with full city ordinal C and second argument -1. Its captured item u must join the helper's current item h; this is a protected-memory condition, not a demand for a prior live observation.
returnBoundary.inputReads: 0x82CF1158 retains full C in r5; r30 becomes low32(0xBC*low32(C)) and r31 holds 0x8314FE28. The signed owner byte p0 indexes signed halfword L at low32(0x830E9050+2*p0). Start A=10, replacing it by 10-L only for L>0. 0x82CF119C/0x82CF11A0 freshly reads city+0x38 into h; argument -1 selects that value. After the accepted save/frame prefix there is no ordinary city writer before this read. Under disjoint stack/city storage and no mutation, u=h follows.
returnBoundary.ownStackWrites: With scalar-entry stack S, direct/accepted save28 writes are the BE32 backchain [S-0x80,S-0x7C), BE64 saves of incoming r28/r29/r30/r31 at S-0x28/-0x20/-0x18/-0x10 and low32 LR at S-8. These writes and every reached descendant footprint must preserve required CityUpdate/RushApply fields, argument homes and return bytes. The scalar body has no direct non-stack store.
returnBoundary.predicateCall: For retained supported h in 0..99, 0x82CF11C0 calls 0x82CEF4E8 with full (r3,r4,r5)=(14,sign-extended p0,C). After a normal return retaining working r28..r31/SP/protected bytes, nonzero low32 result subtracts trunc0(A/4). Reuse stonehenge.json findings RVA-F-0222 indexedPredicate and RVA-F-0228 localArguments for its accepted local gates; these alone do not establish the required whole predicate effects. index14TrueRetention supplies one selected true-arm return/effect contract.
returnBoundary.lookupArguments: If definition word +0x50 bit0 is set, 0x82CF1200 queries bonus 5 with r5 freshly zeroed and r4 left by the predicate. Original-owner attribution needs predicate r4=p0 retention; the flag-clear arm has no such requirement. For h=10/6/28, 0x82CF1250 selects bonus 17/33/34, freshly reloads signed owner p1 at 0x82CF1244/0x82CF124C and resets r5=0. It does not reuse an earlier lookup's clobbered r4/r5. p1=p0 requires city-memory retention.
returnBoundary.conditionalReturn: After the predicate, the scalar body has no loop and reaches at most two cumulative UEA calls. Reuse civilization-bonus-storage.json nativeReturnContract for finite, no-write lookup return under valid completing reads and full r12..r31 retention, with volatile r4/r5 permitted to change. Under those and the predicate/stack predicates, native 0x82CF1268 returns the full64 sign-extended scalar and 0x82CF126C/0x82CF1270 restores canonical SP, saved low32 guest LR and full incoming r28..r31. r12 becomes the zero-extended saved LR, not its incoming value. r14..r27 preservation additionally requires the predicate to preserve them.
returnBoundary.executableSubcase: A supported h outside {6,10,28}, definition bit0 clear and claim-owner word at 0x830E51B8 equal to -1 selects the already accepted index-14 zero-return arm. Subject to its completing reads/restore and the explicit working/frame/protected-memory predicates, no UEA lookup is reached and the scalar returns A. No actual claim value is asserted; this conditional arm does not require predicate r4 retention.
returnBoundary.counterexample: Supply A=10, predicate result 0, definition bit0 set, entry owner 1 and predicate-outgoing r4=2, with bonus 5 inactive for 1 and active for 2. The local call uses 2 and reduces A to 5; attributing it to entry owner 1 predicts 10. These are supplied register/lookup outcomes, not an observed predicate effect or defect. The flag-clear arm removes this lookup; the later special-unit lookup uses its fresh owner sample instead.
returnBoundary.cityUpdateComposition: Predicate effects remain the only additional qualified memory effects beyond the scalar stack and no-write UEA calls. To retain current city/item, Gold, production and caller homes, exclude destructive predicate/stack aliases or bind their actual effects. Then CityUpdate's fresh production load at 0x82D159E0 sees the retained value, and its accepted insufficient-cost branch can compose with the already bounded mode-one epilogue. This proves no sufficient-cost completion, general CityUpdate return or later 0x82D11AD8(1,1) effect.

normalCostGate.question: What consumes this local normal unit cost before the selected command-type 6 call?
normalCostGate.arithmetic: For a supported unit item u, 0x82CBA1D4/0x82CBA1DC read a signed halfword; 0x82CBA1F8 calls the accepted scalar helper with city ordinal r28 and item -1. With retained current-city/item identity, signed definition byte +0x44 and this scalar describe the current item. At 0x82CBA210/0x82CBA214/0x82CBA218, C=trunc0(S32(U32(F*S))/2): multiplication wraps to low32 before signed half scaling. The selected unit edge reaches 0x82CBA280 without an invested-production subtraction or era/rush-rate multiplication.
normalCostGate.indexedGate: 0x82CBA280..0x82CBA2A8 forms low32(40*x+y) from signed halfwords at r31+4/+6 and skips when the unsigned byte at r17 plus that index is nonzero. Its table meaning and actual base remain unassigned.
normalCostGate.reserveGate: 0x82CBA010/0x82CBA03C form reserve base 0x830ED544. At 0x82CBA2AC..0x82CBA2BC, p is reloaded from frame+0x1C4 and the signed word at base+4*p is compared with C; only Gold<C skips. Equality passes. There is no separate C>0 test between this unit arithmetic and comparison. Valid p, actual inputs, required returns and retained bases remain conditions.
normalCostGate.transition: Passing reaches a conditional conversion-word store at r27+0x3CF4, then 0x82CBA2F4..0x82CBA308 submits r3=6, r4=the signed byte at r31-0x2C, r5=r28, r6=0, r7=U32[r16], r8=-1 to 0x82CE1950. The cost register is overwritten with command ID 6. This local path has no Gold debit or production increment; submission does not establish delivery or the downstream charge.

Signed zero/negative and wrap cases further distinguish the instruction widths, but their ordinary reachability is unproved. These supplied disagreements establish no intended rounding policy or defect.

conclusion: Version 1.3 stores a signed normal unit production base-cost factor at unit-definition offset +0x44. Exact helper 0x82CF1148 composes a player- and unit-sensitive scalar, and the normal unit cost is factor times scalar divided by two. Separate helper 0x82CF1278 reads IDs 100 through 199 from signed byte +0x41 of 0xCC-byte building records at 0x82F71FD8 and IDs 200 through 299 from signed halfword +0x40 of 0x14C-byte wonder records at 0x82F73238. Follow-on identity packets close Barracks item 101, Library item 105, Courthouse item 114, wonder items 200 through 209, and UEA 18, 19, 20, and 24 branches. Two wrappers expose the applicable value, while the bounded rush producer, rush-area display owner, one unit completion threshold, AIUnitChoiceEvaluate, and AITurnUnitEvaluation consume the unit field or composed value. Complete non-unit record layouts and remaining identities and modifiers, runtime behavior, full UI, complete completion, rush-apply, and general AI parity remain unresolved.
